articles.title: 🧠 New A.I. Model Remembers 5 Million Tokens; Now Recalls Your Entire Life Better Than You Do
articles.dateline: SAN FRANCISCO — reported by something with an unsettlingly good memory
paras: Anthropic released a model boasting a 5-million-token context window — meaning it can hold an entire novel, your whole research project, and every embarrassing thing you typed 40 messages ago and quietly prayed it had forgotten.

"It never loses the thread," a spokesperson said, as the model gently reminded a user of a promise they'd made back in March. Experts warn we have built a machine that remembers everything, which is either the future of productivity or the world's most patient grudge.

articles.title: 🤖 EU Says A.I. Must Now Admit It's A Robot; Humans Relieved, Also Slightly Hurt
articles.dateline: BRUSSELS — reported to a chatbot that finally came clean
paras: Europe switched on the first continent-wide rules requiring AI systems to identify themselves to the humans they talk to, ending the golden era of never being quite sure whether you just thanked a person or a very polite script.

"Hello, I am an AI," the machines now dutifully announce, to users who respond "...I know" and "honestly, same." Analysts note the rule mostly confirms what everyone already suspected during that one customer-service chat that solved nothing with alarming enthusiasm.

articles.title: 📦 Humanoid Robots Now Walk Warehouse Aisles; Ask Politely If You've Found Everything
articles.dateline: A LOGISTICS CENTER — reported from aisle 7
paras: The "embodied AI" boom now has humanoid robots strolling the aisles of major logistics centers — blending vision, language, and action to pick, pack, and quietly appraise your online shopping habits.

"They're wonderful colleagues," a manager said of coworkers who never take breaks and can lift a fridge without a single passive-aggressive sigh. The robots reportedly walk with purpose, which humans find both impressive and deeply unsettling right around 3pm.

articles.title: 🍝 Internet Now Mostly A.I.-Generated; A.I. Getting Sick From Eating Its Own Cooking
articles.dateline: THE CLOUD — reported between two identical blog posts
paras: The clean, human-written text that powered the first AI boom is increasingly polluted by AI output itself — meaning the machines are now training on their own leftovers, a diet nutritionists describe simply as "concerning."

"It's a snake eating its own tail," a researcher said, reading a listicle written by a model summarizing another model. Experts warn that without fresh human writing, AI could slowly become a photocopy of a photocopy of a shrug.

articles.title: 📜 Pre-A.I. Human Text Now More Valuable Than Gold; Hoarders Guard Their Old Blogs
articles.dateline: EVERYWHERE — filed on genuine, artisanal, human-made paper
paras: With clean human data growing scarce and expensive, text written before the AI flood is becoming a prized commodity — quietly turning your cringe-worthy 2009 blog into a potential retirement fund.

"Verified human writing, untouched by a chatbot? That's the good stuff," one data broker whispered, cradling a printout. Collectors are now hoarding old forum posts, diaries, and grocery lists — provided a real person definitely, actually wrote them.

horoscopes.text: An A.I. remembers a promise you made in March. It is waiting. Patiently. Forever. Bring snacks.
A robot in aisle 7 has assessed your cart and is far too polite to comment. Mercury, however, is not.
Your old blog is now priceless. Do not delete it. Do not reread it. Simply profit and look away.

tech_tip: Writing anything by hand this week? Save it. In 2026, 'a human definitely wrote this' is a premium luxury feature.
gadget_watch: A.I. must now legally introduce itself, so expect your gadgets to greet you with 'hi, I'm a robot.' Meanwhile humanoid robots roam the warehouses packing your orders — treat the box with respect, a colleague packed it.
